biggest_catch: PlaybookUX's official pages are researcher-facing: its 'Automated Payments' is a tool for clients to pay participants, not published worker pay - tester pay figures come only from third parties.
catches: No official concrete tester pay figures: '$10 per unmoderated session' and '$30/$60/$90 for moderated interviews' come from third-party guides.
No official tester payout schedule found.
PlaybookUX's official payment feature is for researchers paying participants - it publishes no worker pay terms.
Tester availability is invite-based with profile screening.

c1.evidence: PlaybookUX's official pages describe 'Automated Payments' as a researcher feature ('Pay and manage incentives for both PlaybookUX panel participants and your own recruits'); no official concrete tester pay figures published.

c2.evidence: No official tester payout schedule found in PlaybookUX's official materials.

c4.evidence: Fails both the official-pay and official-timing requirements.

eligibility: Join the PlaybookUX panel; complete your profile; be selected for studies matching your profile.
maximize: PlaybookUX is rejected here because its official pages publish no concrete tester pay figures and no tester payout schedule. If official tester terms ever publish them, the per-test-type structure third-party guides describe ($10 unmoderated, $30–$90 moderated) maps to 10–90 minute sessions - but these figures are unverified here.
notes: PlaybookUX is a legitimate UX research tool, but its official site is researcher-facing. All tester pay figures in circulation come from third-party guides, not official pages.
